summary.en: Rebel and SPLA-IO forces have intensified attacks across South Sudan, killing civilians in Tonj East, Warrap State, and other locations, with recent incidents reporting 24 deaths including children and women. Cattle-theft raids have also turned lethal, leaving dozens dead and prompting fear of missing persons after assaults on islands such as Miny Island in Jonglei. The violence has spread to the political sphere, with the brother of former Juba Mayor James Allah-Jabu dying and the former vice president Igga announcing the death. The crisis now includes large-scale killings reported in Ruweng and ongoing insecurity ahead of the postponed 2026 election. According to UCDP, there were 2 battle-related deaths in 2024.
summary.nb: Rebel- og SPLA-IO-styrker har økt angrepene over hele Sør-Sudan, og har drept sivile i Tonj East i Warrap-stat og andre steder, med nylige hendelser som rapporterer 24 døde, inkludert barn og kvinner. Kvegtyveri-raider har også blitt dødelige, og har etterlatt dusinvis av døde og skapt frykt for savnede etter angrep på øyer som Miny Island i Jonglei. Voldshandlingene har også nådd den politiske arenaen, da broren til den tidligere Juba-ordføreren James Allah-Jabu er død, og den tidligere visepresidenten Igga kunngjorde dødsfallet. Krisen omfatter nå store drap i Ruweng og vedvarende usikkerhet før det utsatte valget i 2026. Ifølge UCDP var det 2 dødsfall i kamper i 2024.

background.title: South Sudanese Civil War
background.extract: The South Sudanese Civil War was a multi-sided civil war in South Sudan fought from 2013 to 2018 between government and opposition forces. The civil war caused rampant human rights abuses, including forced displacement, ethnic massacres, and killings of journalists by various parties. Since the war's end, South Sudan has been governed by a coalition formed by leaders of the former warring factions, Salva Kiir and Riek Machar. The country continues to recover from the war while experiencing ongoing and systemic ethnic violence.
